name: Saudi Pak Tower
assumptions: Tower plan is about 41 by 26 m, read from the Esri roof; the OSM outline (31 m wide) is narrower than the roof, so the tower overhangs it on both long sides.
Shaft top 64.5 m and module 19.3 m fitted to the architect's photo at 72 m total height (dossier); floor lines are not modelled because the shafts read as blind stone.
Podium 48 by 35 m in plan and 15 m high, positions along its long side mapped linearly from the architect's photo (perspective ignored).
Roof storey plan and position, the courtyard size and its depth are estimates from the Esri tile and one photo.
The SW face is taken as the deep jali stack and the SE face as the shallow arched strip, from reading two photos against the Esri orientation.
The NE and NW faces were not seen by day; their central strips are drawn as glazing with 19 plain floor bars between the same shafts, the NW side has no podium.
Podium NE side copies the SW side; its SE end portal and windows are the plainest match to the two side photos, not seen head-on.
Stone hex #D6C8AE from day photos, replacing the dossier's night estimate #C9A676; blue tile hex is a photo estimate.
The roof disc is plain green with a blue rim; the company emblem and the podium sign lettering are not reproduced.
Jali is simplified to a square grid inside the pointed arch; the true pattern is finer and geometric.
